basis: Migne prints his own reference to Genesis 2:25 inside this answer, which asks 'Inter. 59. Quare non erubescebant Adam et Eva, dum nudi erant (Gen. II, 25)?-- Resp. Quia'. The extent is that reference and nothing wider.
date_basis: The dedicatory letter addresses Sigewulf, Alcuin's pupil and his successor at Tours, and says the questions are ones Sigewulf had put to him over a long acquaintance and are now gathered. Alcuin was abbot of Tours from 796 until his death in 804. The work is conventionally placed in the Tours years and near their beginning; the range records that and no more. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1851 printing, and it is not the seventh century the wiki header gives, which is a century out.
text: Inter. 59. Quare non erubescebant Adam et Eva, dum nudi erant (Gen. II, 25)?-- Resp. Quia nullam legem senserunt in membris suis repugnantem legi mentis suae: nihil enim putabant velandum, quia nihil senserunt refrenandum. Nam in poenam peccati evenit homini, ut ipsa sua caro rebellis ei esset in motibus suis, quia ipse rebellis erat creatori suo in actibus suis.
